![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14221452/assets/b0d11e89592cad64ebbeb72def6ca0a6c5880a9a54f82b394d7857e142c05edf.png)

Find the area bounded between the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x={t}^{3}-4t,\,y={t}^{2}-1
$$

and the $x$-axis for $t\in [0,1].$
question.worked_solution:
The unsigned area bounded by the parametric curve 

$$
x=x(t),\,y=y(t),\,{t}_{1}\le t\le {t}_{2}
$$

and the $x$-axis is given by the absolute value of the integral

$$
{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}-4t) \\  & =3{t}^{2}-4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the integral expression

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({t}^{2}-1)(3{t}^{2}-4)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(3{t}^{4}-7{t}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that this integral will give us a positive number since $y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\ge 0$ for all $t\in [0,1].$

Therefore, the area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(3{t}^{4}-7{t}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}t \\  & =3{\int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{4}\,\text{d}t-7{\int }_{0}^{1}{t}^{2}\,\text{d}t+4{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}t \\  & =3\cdot {\frac{{t}^{5}}{5}\,|}_{0}^{1}-7\cdot {\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}\,|}_{0}^{1}+4\cdot t\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =3(\frac{1}{5}-0)-7(\frac{1}{3}-0)+4(1-0) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}-\frac{7}{3}+4 \\  & =\frac{34}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
